title: Castillos et al. 2023, m-sequence c-VEP, 100% amplitude depth: Burst c-VEP Based BCI: Optimizing stimulus design for enhanced classification with minimal calibration data and improved user experience
description: EEG recordings from 12 healthy participants performing an offline 4-class code-modulated visual evoked potential (c-VEP) reactive BCI task. The study compares burst c-VEP and m-sequence stimulation at 100% and 40% amplitude depth. This subset contains the m-sequence condition at 100% amplitude depth. The data were recorded with a 32-channel system at 500 Hz and used to evaluate CNN-based classification with minimal calibration data, as well as user experience measures such as visual comfort.
methods_description: EEG was recorded with a BrainProducts LiveAmp 32-channel active electrode system at 500 Hz. Participants focused on four targets cued sequentially in random order (0.5 s cue, 2.2 s stimulation, 0.7 s inter-trial interval) across 15 blocks of 4 trials per condition. Stimuli were shown on a 60 Hz LCD monitor. Decoding used a CNN with 250 ms sliding windows, and subjective ratings of comfort, tiredness and intrusiveness were collected.
